What would be a good time to aim for? Currently I can get to about 5-6 minutes on rested legs, considering I am not super into fitness I feel pretty good about my wall sit time but I'm curious as to what some of you fitness people usually shoot for in wall sit times.

What are your fitness goals here? While 5 minutes is pretty good for wall sits, they're still not effective use of your training time unless you're a skier or something. Wall sits don't build mass, or burn a lot of calories.

Training barbell squats would be more effective for most goals, and if you don't have access to barbells than you might consider either training bodyweight squats for reps or learning to do a single-leg squat.

Jackie Chan reported having to do wall sits for several hours as part of some crazy Chinese acrobat training. The limit is mostly based on mental toughness and something called rhabdomyolysis.

Hmm. I'm more interested in building a little more upper body mass than anything else. I've only been doing wall sits largely because I felt like I was neglecting my legs too much and I wanted to make sure I regularly did something about that. Mostly I just want to shed a bit of body fat % so my abs come through more clearly. I've only got access to a set of free weights and a chin up bar. I never really considered the possibility that something isn't an effective use of my training time. I just find cardio annoying and I loved the feeling in my legs I get when I did wall sits.

My last fitness goal was to do 100 pushups at one time, which I did about a year ago, since then I've just been making sure I don't become a fatty.

I remember watching something about this lady who was trying to go for a wall sit world record. I'm not terribly surprised that it comes down to mental toughness considering how long some people can go for, I find it a lot easier to hit my 5 minute mark if I'm feeling pumped up.

The hormonal response from weighted squats will help with putting on mass more than the other methods I suggested, even on the upper-body.

Anyway, taking a shot in the dark here, I think you'll like this routine. I'm guessing you prefer to work out almost every day, judging from your hundred push-ups program, and I sense some reluctance to use weights or go to a gym.

Adding a hip-hinge movement, like a deadlift, glute-ham curl, or a sliding bridge curl to B-days will help, A regular bridge can replace the weird "prone cobra" position he advocates, and I prefer hanging leg raises over floor leg raises. Throw in some kind of overhead-push movement on A days, either some form of handstand-push-up or military press, and suddenly you have a balanced, comprehensive, full-body routine. He has a three day version on his website somewhere too.

Or you could do Starting Strength or Stronglifts 5*5, but they don't need a lot of customization. Feel free to PM me if you have any questions you don't feel like asking here.

You got it dead on. I used to work out every few days but recently I've been working out nearly every day. I don't go to the gym because I hate driving, which is another thing entirely. But the point is you are right, I prefer not to go to the gym, I've always been biased towards workouts that I don't need equipment for because it means I can do them anywhere.
